title: Intergenerational Trauma
subtitle: How adversity can affect later generations through multiple pathways
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical neuroscience diagram illustrating intergenerational trauma across threat, memory, regulation and treatment systems.
learningObjectives: Explain intergenerational trauma in clinically accurate language.
Distinguish established findings from theoretical or mixed claims in intergenerational trauma.
Identify one limitation or safety implication relevant to intergenerational trauma.

sections.explainSimply: Trauma can influence families through caregiving, beliefs, stress exposure, social conditions and possibly biological pathways.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Intergenerational associations are supported across psychological, family and physiological outcomes, but human studies cannot cleanly separate caregiving, social and structural transmission from biological pathways. Epigenetic transmission remains plausible but unproven as a general causal explanation.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Human evidence is observational and vulnerable to shared-environment, historical, socioeconomic and measurement confounding. Epigenetic differences in descendants do not demonstrate inheritance of a trauma memory, nor do they establish an inevitable biological destiny.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Think of intergenerational trauma as one part of a dynamic safety-and-learning system rather than a single switch.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need intergenerational trauma to connect symptoms with learning, context, risk and treatment choice without reducing the person to a brain scan.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Avoid deterministic claims that trauma is genetically “passed down.”
sections.clinicalPearl: Clinical pearl: use intergenerational trauma to sharpen formulation, not to replace phenomenology or outcome measurement.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician uses intergenerational trauma to formulate triggers, state shifts, avoidance and functional impact, then monitors whether intervention improves daily life rather than relying on presumed neural change.
sections.limitationsCautions: Avoid deterministic claims that trauma is genetically or epigenetically “passed down.” Evidence classification: intergenerational associations are supported; specifically epigenetic transmission in humans remains limited and contested.
